title: libsrt SndQ sampled-stack profile: per-destination multiplexers vs lane multiplexer groups

host.perf: linux-tools 6.8, software cpu-clock event (hardware counters not exposed)

load.source: 8 Mbit/s MPEG-TS published live with ffmpeg -re -c copy
load.hls: on (the pre-fix build only prepares TS for SRT with HLS on)

classification: sched/wakeup = context switch, wake and futex paths, scheduler entry/exit; send path = sendmsg, UDP/IP transmit, skb and copy; other = the rest (libsrt bookkeeping, locks)
finding: The per-destination SndQ cost is scheduler work: 61.7 of 90.4 %core is context switching and wakeups, against 11.0 in the send path.  Sharing a lane's multiplexer removes 42.6 of the 51.6 points saved from the wakeup path; the send path is nearly unchanged (11.0 -> 9.0), as it should be for the same bytes.
reproduce: tests: /tmp driver in the commit message; perf record -F 499 -g -p <worker> -- sleep 15, then perf report --sort comm,sym -n
